passage: My name is Harsha, and for three months Gargi has messaged me at all hours. Last night her voice note arrived at 1 a.m., and I listened with my eyes half shut because I had a chemistry test at eight. I love her. She told me something heavy about her home and said I was the only one she could trust. But lately I answer with just "hmm" and "ok", and then feel guilty and resentful in the same breath. Today I finally said, "I want to be there for you, but I can't be your only person, and I can't reply after ten." She looked hurt. I suggested her aunt, and the school counsellor too. She said she would think about it.

qa.q: What time did Gargi's voice note arrive last night?
qa.a: Her voice note arrived at 1 a.m.

qa.q: What was Harsha feeling about the late-night messages, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Harsha was worn out and a little resentful while still caring; the "hmm" and "ok" replies and the guilt in the same breath show it.

qa.q: What would you advise Harsha to do if Gargi keeps messaging late at night?
qa.a: Keep the limit kindly, and gently repeat the idea of talking to her aunt or the school counsellor.

qa.q: How might Gargi have felt when Harsha set the limit?
qa.a: Gargi looked hurt, and may have feared losing the one person she trusts, though saying she would think about it shows the idea did not fall on deaf ears.

grounding: Harsha is worn out by a friend's constant heavy confiding, sets a limit and points to a counsellor and family.

passage:
Hostel warden's note, senior block, Tuesday

Dolma has been falling asleep in morning prep all week. When I asked, she showed me her phone: forty-two messages from Kunal between midnight and three, most of them about his parents' arguments at home and whether his marks are good enough. She said she answers every one because he is her closest friend and she does not want him to feel alone.

She also said, very quietly, "Sometimes I start to hate seeing his name." Then she looked ashamed of saying it.

We talked about how caring for a friend does not mean being on call all night. She decided to tell him she will reply until ten and after breakfast, and that she still cares. She also wanted him to have more people than just her. With her permission, I spoke to the school counsellor, who will meet Kunal tomorrow. I have asked Dolma to come back on Friday and tell me how the week went.

qa.q: How many messages did Kunal send between midnight and three?
qa.a: Kunal sent forty-two messages between midnight and three.

qa.q: What does Dolma's quiet comment about Kunal's name suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Dolma is exhausted and starting to feel resentful, and then ashamed of that feeling because she cares about him.

qa.q: What limit did Dolma decide to set, and why does it help?
qa.a: Dolma decided to reply only until ten and after breakfast, which lets her keep caring for Kunal without losing sleep and growing bitter.

qa.q: How might Kunal feel when Dolma sets the new limit?
qa.a: Kunal might feel hurt or worried at first, but meeting the counsellor could give him more support than one tired friend at night.

grounding: It shows a teen worn out by a friend who leans on her at all hours, who keeps caring while setting limits and bringing in a counsellor.

passage:
Sunday, 11:15 pm

It's happening again. Phone buzzing. Yamini, third call tonight. It's been every night since the breakup, sometimes till one. I love her, I really do. But I fell asleep in the chemistry practical on Friday and Ma'am noticed. And tonight, when her name flashed, the first thing I felt was irritation, and then guilt for feeling it.

I don't want to be the friend who starts avoiding calls and says "sorry, was asleep" every night. That feels worse than being honest.

So I picked up and said it. "Yami, I'm here for you. But I can't talk past ten-thirty on school nights, I'm falling apart. Let's walk together at lunch every day this week instead. And can you please talk to your didi, or Mrs Pinto? You need more than just me."

She was quiet. Then she said, "Okay. Sorry. I didn't notice." She said she would talk to her didi tomorrow.

I feel lighter already.

— Anjali

qa.q: When did Anjali fall asleep in class?
qa.a: Anjali fell asleep in the chemistry practical on Friday.

qa.q: What did Anjali feel when Yamini's name flashed tonight?
qa.a: Anjali felt irritation first and then guilt for feeling it, because Anjali loves Yamini but is exhausted.

qa.q: What would you say Anjali got right in the phone call?
qa.a: Anjali was honest about a limit, offered another way to be there at lunch, and pointed Yamini to her didi and Mrs Pinto.

qa.q: How might Yamini see Anjali's limit?
qa.a: Yamini may feel a bit embarrassed at not noticing, but also still cared for, since Anjali offered daily lunch walks.

grounding: It shows a teen worn out by a friend who calls every night, who cares, sets a limit and encourages other support instead of quietly resenting the friend.
